full_judgment: 7. Mr Abdul Quayum, learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners, submits that since the instant suit is not maintainable being hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, the trial Court rightly dismissed the same and the appellate Court below committed an error of law by decreeing the same when it was liable to be dismissed in limini. The learned Advocate elaborating his augment submits that the plaintiff-opposite parties had no locus standi to file the present suit inasmuch as they could not be said to have any legal character or right to property in respect of the suit land inasmuch as SA Khatian standing in their names had no presumptive value as regards proprietary right to the suit land. It is also contended by the learned Advocate that the suit is not maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as the plaintiff-opposite parties failed to seek any declaration as to their own status and also failed to pray for a further or consequential relief by way of possession. In support of his aforesaid submissions the learned Advocate referred to and relied on the cases reported in 18 DLR 706, to show that the plaintiff must have legal character or right to property, 6 BCR (AD) 57 showing that mere declaration in the absence of consequential relief is fatal, 42 DLR 24 and 13 DLR 676 showing that symbolical possession by defendant requires plaintiff to seek relief for recovery of possession. The learned Advocate also relied on the case reported in 19 DLR 9 in support of his contention that the SA Khatian does not give rise to any presumption of title to the suit land.
